title: approvals: the stranded-request inspector reads 500 unordered decided rows, so past 500 it stops seeing new strands
body:
repo:objectstack#2 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgV6i8jfWwSXjpWJrjA

Filing gate: ① (named location, read on `main` 6e8f6637, not run: a `finding` for triage) · Source: fleet (#37767 design note, section 8, reviewed)

## What happens

`#inspectStrandedRequests` in `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts` runs on the five-minute escalation sweep. Each time, it reads up to 500 rows of every request that is `approved`, `rejected` or `returned`, with no order and no cursor. Once a deployment has more than 500 decided requests, the page it reads is arbitrary, so a newly stranded request may never be inspected. Its output goes only to a log line.

## Expected

The inspector reads only the rows that can be stranded: a store-filterable mark, or the newest decided requests ordered with a cursor. A pin with more than 500 decided rows shows that a new strand is still reported. #37767 (ADR-0162 item 8) makes this reader load-bearing for closed-state documents, so it should be fixed before or with that build.

Reach: every deployment with more than 500 decided approval requests. Reproduce first, since this is read, not run.
Reader: triage → the approvals lane, or fold into #37767's build if triage routes it there.
Grade: suggested p2.
Dedupe: searched open issues for `inspectStrandedRequests`: 0 hits.
Related: #37767, ADR-0162.
